title: Selection Sort
directAnswer: For each position i, scan i..n-1 for the minimum index, then swap it into position i. O(n²) comparisons, at most n swaps.

remember.takeaway: Selection sort minimises swaps at the cost of always O(n²) compares.
remember.formula: for i: m=argmin(a[i..]); swap a[i], a[m]

problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, sort it ascending using selection sort (in place).
understanding: Repeatedly find the minimum of the unsorted suffix and swap it to the front of that suffix.

approaches.name: Select-min and swap
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Selection sort grows a sorted prefix by repeatedly **finding the minimum** of the unsorted suffix and swapping it to the front of that suffix.

**Why track the min index, not swap eagerly.** Scan the suffix recording the index of the smallest element, then do a single swap into position i. Swapping every time you see a smaller value would do many extra writes.

**Its signature property: few swaps.** It always does O(n²) *comparisons*, but only O(n) *swaps* (one per position). When writes are expensive (e.g. to flash memory), that minimal-write property is its advantage over bubble sort.

**Not stable, in place.** It can reorder equal elements, and uses O(1) extra space. Like the other O(n²) sorts, it's a fundamentals algorithm.
hints: Each step places which element into its final spot?
Find the min index of the suffix, then swap once.
Compare its swap count to bubble sort's.
approaches.complexityReasoning: n positions each scanning the remaining suffix → O(n²) comparisons, but only O(n) swaps.

java.explanation: Track the index of the smallest remaining element.
Place the minimum at the front of the unsorted part.

dryRun.intro: Select the min, swap to front.

edgeCases.behavior: Still O(n²) comparisons even when sorted.

pitfalls: Swapping values instead of tracking the min index.
Starting the inner scan at i instead of i+1 (harmless but wasteful).

commonMistakes: Swapping values instead of tracking the min index.
Starting the inner scan at i instead of i+1 (harmless but wasteful).

clarifyingQuestions.question: Stability required?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Selection sort isn't stable; I'd pick insertion/merge sort if it is.
